sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module overview and imports
sections.what: Nothing runs here. It describes the three statements and the balance check, and loads a helper.
sections.why: Gives the reader the big picture before the code.

sections.name: build_income_statement
sections.title: Income statement from sales to net income
sections.what: Takes yearly revenue, costs, expenses, depreciation, interest, and tax, and works down to gross profit, EBITDA, EBIT, pretax income, and net income.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is the standard layout that shows profit at each stage.
sections.watch_out: Lists are matched by position and stop at the shortest one, so unequal lengths silently drop years.

sections.name: build_cash_flow_statement (part 1)
sections.title: Operating, investing and financing cash flows
sections.what: Works out operating cash flow by adding back depreciation and taking off the working capital increase, then works out investing and financing cash flows.
sections.why: Depreciation is not a cash payment, so it is added back. The working capital increase ties up cash, so it is taken off.
sections.watch_out: The padding used to line up the working capital list drops the change for the final year.

sections.name: build_cash_flow_statement (part 2)
sections.title: Net cash change and running cash total
sections.what: Adds the three cash flows for each year to get the net change, then adds those changes into a running cash balance.
sections.why: The cash line on the balance sheet comes from this running total.
sections.watch_out: The running total starts at zero, so the cash balance is only right if the company truly begins with no cash.

sections.name: build_balance_sheet (part 1)
sections.title: Assets, liabilities and equity calculation
sections.what: Adds up assets and liabilities, works out equity as whatever is left over, and computes the balance check.
sections.why: The code comment says equity is the plug that makes the sheet balance.
sections.watch_out: Because equity is forced to balance, the balance check always returns zero and proves nothing.

sections.name: build_balance_sheet (part 2)
sections.title: Returning the balance sheet lines
sections.what: Packages every balance sheet line into one result.
sections.why: Gives the caller all the balance sheet lines in one place.
sections.watch_out: The starting equity setting is accepted but never used, so it has no effect.

sections.name: build_three_statement_model (part 1)
sections.title: Gathering inputs and building the first two statements
sections.what: Pulls the needed lists from the other modules and builds the income statement and cash flow statement.
sections.why: Acts as the single entry point that connects the modules.
sections.watch_out: It relies on exact key names and on the revenue result being a pair, so a renamed key or changed return shape causes an error.

sections.name: build_three_statement_model (part 2)
sections.title: Building the balance sheet and returning results
sections.what: Builds the balance sheet from cash, working capital, net assets, and debt, then returns all three statements.
sections.why: Completes the set of three statements.
sections.watch_out: The balance sheet inherits the plug equity described earlier, so a passing balance check here does not show the model is correct.

summary: Combines the calculation parts into three linked financial statements (income statement, cash flow statement, and balance sheet) for each year, with a balance check.
purpose: Produces the three statements and the balance check that is meant to confirm they agree.
why: The three statements are the final picture of the company's finances, and they must agree with each other.
how: 1. Build the income statement from revenue, costs, expenses, depreciation, interest, and tax. 2. Build the cash flow statement from net income, depreciation, working capital, capital spending, and debt. 3. Build the balance sheet from cash, receivables, stock, net assets, payables, and debt. 4. Calculate equity as the balancing figure. 5. Return all three statements.
inputs: Result dictionaries from the revenue, cost, expense, capital spending, working capital, debt, and tax modules.
outputs: A dictionary holding income_statement, cash_flow_statement, and balance_sheet, each a dictionary of yearly lists.
risks: Equity is calculated as assets minus liabilities, so the balance check always shows zero and cannot catch errors. The working capital change in the final year is dropped from cash flow. Opening cash is taken as zero and the starting equity input is ignored. Capital spending and debt repayments are expected as positive numbers, though some docstrings describe them as negative.
debug: Do not rely on the balance check alone, since it always passes. Compare the cash balance line with the balance sheet cash line year by year. For a gap in the final year, look at the working capital change in that year. Confirm each input list has the same length.
